title: Psoriasis Severity Stratification
subtitle: BSA / PASI / DLQI → therapy class decision tree

steps.prompt: Patient presents with plaque psoriasis. Assess BSA, PASI, and DLQI.

steps.detail: First-line: high-potency topical corticosteroid (class I–II) ± vitamin D analog (calcipotriene/calcitriol). Use calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) for sensitive sites (face, intertriginous). Reassess at 4–8 weeks.
Taper to lowest effective frequency. Vitamin D analogs can be used long-term; tachyphylaxis limits prolonged steroid use. Reassess annually.

steps.prompt: Moderate psoriasis — assess for special sites and comorbidities

branches.label: PsA, IBD, or oral systemic preferred
Refractory or special site with DLQI impact

steps.detail: Narrowband UVB (NB-UVB) is preferred for widespread plaque psoriasis; 3× weekly, expect response at 20–30 sessions. PUVA for palmoplantar disease. Excimer laser for limited/localized disease. Continue topicals as adjunct.

Methotrexate 10–25 mg/week (oral or SC): first-choice systemic; also beneficial for PsA. Apremilast 30 mg BID (PDE4 inhibitor): favorable safety, no lab monitoring. Cyclosporine 2.5–5 mg/kg/day: rapid onset, use as short bridge ≤1 year due to nephrotoxicity/hypertension. Acitretin for pustular/erythrodermic variants.

steps.prompt: Step up to biologic — screen first
steps.detail: Complete baseline workup: CBC, CMP, LFTs, lipids, HBV/HCV/HIV serology, QuantiFERON-TB Gold. Update vaccinations before starting. Then select biologic by comorbidity profile.

IL-23 p19 inhibitors (guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab) are preferred for plaque psoriasis: highest PASI 90/100 rates, Q8–12 week dosing, favorable safety profile. IL-17 inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) if rapid clearance needed or concurrent PsA. TNF-α inhibitors if comorbid IBD or cost constraints. Topicals remain adjunctive.

steps.prompt: Special site psoriasis — escalate if DLQI impacted
steps.detail: Scalp: high-potency steroid solution/foam ± calcipotriene scalp solution; shampoo formulations. Nail: intralesional triamcinolone to nail matrix, topical calcipotriene under occlusion; biologic if severe. Genital/face: low-potency steroid or calcineurin inhibitor. If DLQI >5, treat as at least moderate disease.

Prefer IL-17 inhibitors (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) or IL-23 inhibitors (guselkumab, risankizumab) — both have PsA indication. TNF-α inhibitors (adalimumab, certolizumab, etanercept, infliximab, golimumab) remain valid. Apremilast for mild-moderate PsA. Avoid IL-17 if concurrent IBD.

Prefer TNF-α inhibitors (adalimumab, infliximab, certolizumab) — have IBD indications. AVOID IL-17 inhibitors (can exacerbate IBD). IL-23 inhibitors generally safer (risankizumab approved for Crohn's). Avoid cyclosporine in combination with IBD biologics.
AVOID TNF-α inhibitors (may demyelinate/worsen MS). Prefer IL-17, IL-23 inhibitors, or apremilast. Methotrexate can be used. Consult neurology before initiating biologic therapy.

Psoriasis independently increases MACE risk. IL-23 and IL-17 inhibitors appear cardiovascular-neutral or beneficial. Avoid cyclosporine (hypertension, dyslipidemia). Methotrexate may have modest cardioprotective benefit. Deucravacitinib (TYK2) has limited long-term CV data.

Certolizumab pegol (TNF-α inhibitor): preferred biologic — PEGylated Fc-free, minimal placental transfer (Category B equivalent). Avoid methotrexate, acitretin (teratogenic — washout required). Narrowband UVB is safe in pregnancy. Topical low-potency steroids and emollients acceptable. If postpartum breastfeeding, certolizumab is also preferred.

Assess PASI and DLQI at 12–16 weeks. Target: PASI 90 (preferred) or ≥75% improvement. If inadequate, switch within or across class. Annual monitoring: CBC, CMP, LFTs, TB surveillance, injection-site reactions. Screen for new comorbidities annually.

citations.quote: Menter A et al. Joint AAD-NPF guidelines of care for management of psoriasis with biologics. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2020.
Strober B et al. Psoriasis comorbidities and implications for therapy. NEJM. 2020.
